title: American Revolution
examples: What were the main reasons the colonists wanted to separate?
What important documents were created during the Revolution?
How did the war change the American colonies?

explain.say: The first main cause was the taxes placed on the colonies.
Another cause was the desire for self-governance from the colonists.
The British enforcing trade rules also caused much frustration.
The Declaration of Independence explained the colonists' reasons for leaving.
The outcome was the creation of a new, independent nation.
In everyday life, think about using a shared family computer.

faq.q: Why did the colonists feel the taxes were unfair?
faq.a: They felt the taxes were unfair because they had no elected representatives in the British Parliament to vote on those taxes. Asks: Why no say in Parliament? What does 'no representation' mean?
asks: Did they have a say in the laws?

faq.q: What was the main purpose of the Declaration of Independence?
faq.a: Its main purpose was to formally announce that the colonies were separating from Great Britain and establishing themselves as free states. Asks: What did the Declaration do? Why write a declaration?

faq.q: Did the Americans win the war easily?
faq.a: No, the war was long and difficult, involving many battles against the powerful British army. Asks: Was it an easy war? Who fought them?

faq.q: What did 'self-governance' mean for the colonists?
faq.a: It meant they wanted the right to make their own laws and govern themselves without constant control from Britain. Asks: What is self-governance? Do they want to rule themselves?
asks: What did they want to control?
What does it mean to govern oneself?

faq.q: Were there any groups that disagreed with the Revolution?
faq.a: Yes, some colonists remained loyal to the British Crown, which caused internal conflict. Asks: Were all colonists on the same page? Who stayed with the King?

facts: The Stamp Act was a direct tax on printed materials in the colonies.
The Declaration of Independence was adopted in the year 1776.
The outcome was the formation of the United States of America.
Colonists argued for 'no taxation without representation'.

quiz.say: The colonists protested taxes because they felt:

options.show: They wanted a lower tax rate.
options.say: They wanted a lower tax rate.

options.show: They had no say in the laws.
options.say: They had no say in the laws.

quiz.why: This shows they felt powerless against distant rule.

wrong.0: The problem was not the amount, but who decided the amount.
wrong.1: This suggests an alternative payment method, but the issue was legal authority.
wrong.3: While taxes were an issue, the core argument was about the right to vote.

quiz.say: What key document formally declared separation from Britain?
quiz.why: This document was the formal announcement of their new status.

wrong.0: This treaty ended the war, but the Declaration started the process.
wrong.2: This document came later and established a weaker government structure.
wrong.3: This was an event of protest, not the declaration itself.

quiz.say: If a colony wanted to rule itself, what concept were they seeking?
quiz.why: Autonomy means self-rule, which was their main goal.

wrong.0: Loyalism was the group that opposed self-rule and stayed with Britain.
wrong.1: Taxation was the problem that stopped them from achieving self-rule.
wrong.3: Mercantilism was the economic policy Britain tried to enforce, not what the colonists wanted.
